newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish fund managers see strong demand for issues.
newsitem.headline: Finnish fund managers see strong demand for issues.

text.p: Demand for share issues and new public offerings followed by stock exchange listings is expected to remain strong despite the current jittery market situation, Finnish fund managers said on Thursday.

Sentiment on the Helsinki bourse turned bearish in line with overseas markets in mid-March, after the HEX general index had gained some 20 percent in a record-breaking streak from the start of the year.
But fund managers said pricing was the key to unleash demand, not necessarily the market sentiment.
"The prospects for issues remain good as long as they are adequately priced," said Evli fund manager Henrik Damsten.
Big chunks of the share issues and IPO's are sold overseas and fund managers said that demand from foreign investors has remained strong.
Alfred Berg fund manager Tim Hermansson said big Finnish companies with foreign ownership were attracting the same investors to invest in smaller firms as well.

"There are several big international companies listed on the Helsinki bourse which have big foreign investors among their owners, and these are the ones who are likely to invest in new offerings as well," he said.
A recent example of a successful listing was cablemaker PK Cables Oy, whose offering of 2.6 million shares was 10 times oversubscribed.
Foreign investors subscribed 31.5 percent of the PK-Cables shares on offer and would have bought a lot more if any had been available, IPO lead manager Carnegie said.
"If it were possible, all of the offerings would go overseas," Damsten said.

Aluminium profiles and components maker Nordic Aluminium is the next in line for a listing. Its initial public offering started on April 9 and is due to end on April 17. Trade in the share is expected to start on April 24.

A further privatisation of steel group Rautaruukki Oy will go ahead this year in a form of a new share issue. The plans are to reduce the Finnish state's ownership to below 50 percent from current 68.7 percent.
